entries.reason: Product-owner-approved M2 retirement of broken legacy audit reminder jobs 4, 5, and 6; tables and helper functions remain in place.

Carl explicitly authorized pausing the nightly stage-health cron (2026-09-07, Phase 2.6 Packet P3-A / H0.0 containment) since the current metric is known-defective and superseded by the new client-health plan. stage_health_snapshots table and the run-stage-health-monitor Edge Function are retained.

Carl explicitly authorized M3-C after the dependency cross-check: notification_schedule is empty and has no foreign-key, function, view, trigger, or cron dependants; legacy queue and email writers are retired. The active notification_audit_log and notification_outbox tables are preserved.

Carl explicitly authorized retiring the active workload forecast schedule after M4 preflight confirmed snapshots exist but burn/risk/retention forecast outputs are empty. The Edge Function and all snapshot/forecast tables are retained for evidence and a separately approved Client Health replacement.
Manual, disabled-by-default rollback for M4 schedule retirement; requires explicit session settings and an operator decision before restoring the workload cron.

Carl explicitly authorized retiring forecast jobs 20 and 21 after M4 preflight confirmed both output tables are empty. The migration only unschedules the exact named jobs and retains all functions, tables, and rows for Client Health replacement.
Manual, disabled-by-default rollback for M4 forecast cron retirement; requires explicit session settings and an operator decision before restoring either schedule.

False positive: the flagged INSERT/UPDATE statements are inside CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bodies for get_user_notification_prefs/update_user_notification_prefs (only executed later, per-caller, when those RPCs run) - the migration itself performs no direct data mutation, only ALTER COLUMN DROP NOT NULL, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, and two function redefinitions. Carl explicitly authorized proceeding with the not-null fix after reviewing the tenant-assignment question separately (L10 #18, parked to docs/kb/reference/tenant-operating-model-data-architecture-plan-2026-09-02.md §18 item 14).

False positive, same shape as p4d-18-allow-tenant-less-notification-prefs above: all 5 flagged INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE statements are inside the CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION body for swap_tenant_user_to_contact (tenant_contacts insert/update, tenant_users delete, audit_eos_events insert, client_timeline_events insert) - unchanged from the function's existing production behavior, only executed later, per-caller, when a tenant admin actually calls the RPC. The migration itself performs no direct data mutation; it only adds one new guard clause (reject p_user_id = auth.uid()) ahead of the existing, unmodified body. Carl explicitly authorized this scoped self-swap-guard hotfix (L10 #31) for review via the standard allowlist path after the scanner flagged the pre-existing function body as new text.

False positive, same shape as l10-31-swap-tenant-user-to-contact-self-guard and p4d-18-allow-tenant-less-notification-prefs above: the flagged 'UPDATE unicorn1.users' statement is inside the CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION body for the new mark_unicorn1_user_mapped(bigint, uuid) RPC - it is not executed at migration-apply time, only later, per-caller, when the mark-unicorn1-user-mapped Edge Function invokes the RPC (gated on FeatureKeys.adminUnicorn1 via requireCaller, same as the existing search_unicorn1_users read-side function this mirrors). The migration itself performs no direct data mutation; it only creates the function and revokes PUBLIC/authenticated/anon EXECUTE. Carl explicitly authorized this L10 #33 hotfix in-session (directed applying the migration, reviewing the follow-up PUBLIC-grant-revoke fix, and instructing the merge) before this allowlist entry was added for the standard CI review path.

False positive, same shape as p4d-18/l10-31/l10-33 above: all flagged INSERT/UPDATE statements are inside the CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bodies for start_client_package and transition_membership_state (package_instances/stage_instances/staff_task_instances/client_task_instances/email_instances/document_instances/client_audit_log inserts, package_instance_state_log insert, package_instances/tenants updates) - unchanged from each function's existing production behavior, only executed later, per-caller, when a SuperAdmin/staff user actually calls the RPC. The migration itself performs no direct data mutation; it only adds an app.user_can_access_tenant() authorization check ahead of each existing, unmodified body, revokes SELECT on two views, creates one new read-only SECURITY DEFINER RPC (get_package_burndown), and drops/recreates get_tenant_user_capacity without its spoofable p_caller_id parameter. Carl explicitly authorized all four fixes ("proceed on all four") after independent live re-verification of each finding by both Claude and Codex, then explicitly authorized the merge. See docs/audit-log/entries/2026-09-11-tenant-package-security-fixes.md.
